analysis:
Documentation-only change. It adds a startup shape-warmup TTFT report (docs/reports/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md), an index entry in docs/reports/README.md (line 7), and one documented environment variable, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, in docs/reference/configuration.md. The configuration row at about line 414 appears only in the patch excerpt; the supplied head text starts at line 515. The rest of the supplied configuration text is unchanged context.

No source code is changed, so no trust-boundary behavior moves in this diff: coordinator-provider WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, X25519 E2E encryption and fan helper are all untouched. The prefix cache (T-041) is unchanged. The report says its benchmarks ran with the prefix cache off and used unique nonces per prompt, so it does not describe any cache or timing-oracle change. Weakening the cache TTL or scoping would need a fresh SEC-035 sign-off, and nothing here does that.

The documented variable is an availability and performance control. It disables a load-time warmup or skips the probe, and it is described as training no rate or counter and being forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The report names evidence files under evidence/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup/ that are not in the supplied units. Their existence and contents are unverified, which is an evidence-completeness gap, not a security issue.

The actual warmup implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupMode, the 20 s bound, and whether warmup input is synthetic or contains no consumer data) is outside this batch. If the same PR contains that code, a later pass should check that warmup uses synthetic inputs only, is bounded, and does not touch the attestation, authorization or cache paths. No findings in this documentation batch.
